AC10: Windows sweep 35551741150 read. The sweep is red overall (1596 distinct failures) and is continue-on-error, so the verdict is per-test, not per-job.

The merged fix (290424c8491) works. In test_copy_rewrites_readonly_linked_worktree_git_pointer the copy now completes and assert_store_self_contained(copied) passes; the production seam routes through the safe in-place rewrite. But the test still failed, and two sibling tests still raised the filed PermissionError on ...\\.tickets-tracker\\.git, so AC10 was not met. Two distinct causes, both now fixed in Gerrit change 3028 (commit 67df29cc4d7):

Class A, assertion only. Line 68 compared str(Path.resolve()), which renders Windows backslashes, against git's gitdir: pointer, which is always forward-slash. Product behaviour was correct; the assertion was separator-naive. Now uses Path.as_posix(), which is identical to str() on POSIX so it is cross-platform safe.

Class B, test helper bypass. test_half_fixed_copy_is_rejected and test_bare_worktree_repair_is_destructive_and_is_rejected built their stores with a raw shutil.copytree plus the module-local _rewrite(), which opens the pointer with Path.write_text(mode='w') and never reaches the fixed production retry. Reproduced on macOS by clearing write bits: direct write_text raises the same PermissionError. Both tests now build through _clone_template. This is test-only: the tracebacks terminate inside the test helper, not in product code.

No product gap remains for the filed defect class.

Three failures in that file are NOT this defect class and are being filed separately: a local-sibling remote relocation failure, a POSIX-mode assertion that Windows reports as 0o666, and a missing ssh-keygen >= 8.9 precondition on the runner.

Local gates: pytest tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py 14 passed; make verify clean with exactly the 17 known macOS-arm64 pandoc failures. Not re-verifiable on live Windows until 3028 merges.

## Windows sweep confirms the fix

Sweep run `35572919806`, job `106248614492` (`sweep (windows)`), against `1b3bf5ffd1f`.

### The target test is absent from the failure set

`test_copy_rewrites_readonly_linked_worktree_git_pointer` appears **0 times** in the entire
311,653-line job log.

Absence only proves something if the test ran, so that was checked rather than assumed. Its
module was demonstrably collected and executed: 4 sibling tests in
`tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` report as FAILED in the same run —

- `test_half_fixed_copy_is_rejected`
- `test_signing_key_keeps_restrictive_mode`
- `test_opcert_signing_key_is_isolated_per_store`
- `test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated`

Those 4 are unrelated pre-existing Windows failures (a `--git-common-dir` precondition, a
mode-widening assertion, absent `ssh-keygen`, and origin repointing), none of them a
`PermissionError`. The module ran; the target test passed.

### The `.tickets-tracker\.git` PermissionError class is empty

All 41 remaining `PermissionError` occurrences in the run land on different paths in
unrelated modules — `.git\objects` (`test_pinned_ticket_view`,
`test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup`), `.rebar\gate_runs`, and `rebar-gate-snapshots`
(`test_snapshot_cache`). None is on a `.tickets-tracker\.git` pointer file.

The fixture defect this ticket describes no longer produces setup failures.

### Why the job is still red, and why that is not this ticket's concern

The `sweep (windows)` job is red overall — `1876 failed, 18314 passed, 282 skipped, 27 errors`
in 1:41:02 — and is `continue-on-error`, so the run's own conclusion is `success`. Windows is
a broad advisory lane, not a gate, so the correct reading is per-test rather than per-job. The
bulk of those failures are distinct pre-existing classes: absent `npm` for the e2e toolchain
tier, Windows path separators defeating `assert 'a/b' in ...` string comparisons, `charmap`
codec errors on non-UTF-8 output, and `Filename too long` on deeply nested pytest tmpdirs.
Those are separate defects and are not claimed by this ticket.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`tests/_topology_template.py` cannot copy a store template on Windows when the source is a
linked worktree whose `.tickets-tracker/.git` is a `gitdir:` pointer file.
`_rewrite_embedded_paths()` reopens the copied marker with `write_bytes`, which raises
`PermissionError`.

In the Windows advisory sweep, that fixture defect accounted for a large class of setup
failures under `.tickets-tracker\.git`.

## The first fix was built on a wrong premise — corrected here

This ticket originally recorded the cause as "the copy preserved the read-only mode". **That
is wrong, and the first fix (landed, Gerrit change 3015) does not resolve the defect.**

Windows sweep run `35530066749` shows the failure at
`tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py:57` — the FIRST `_clone_template` call, which
produces `readonly-source`. That is the test's opening statement, executed before the test
chmods anything, and the traceback's `original` bytes point at the pristine template. The
file was never read-only.

The landed handler did run. Line 205 raised, the `gitdir:` guard matched,
`chmod(mode | stat.S_IWUSR)` executed, and **the retry at line 212 raised the identical
`PermissionError`**. A chmod that does not change the outcome proves the read-only attribute
was not the cause.

## Root cause

`os.chmod` on Windows only toggles `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY`. Git for Windows marks a linked
worktree's `.git` pointer **hidden**, and `open(..., "wb")` maps to Win32 `CREATE_ALWAYS`,
which is refused with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` on a file carrying `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN`.
`chmod` cannot clear HIDDEN, so no amount of permission fixing lifts the refusal.

`open(..., "r+b")` maps to `OPEN_EXISTING`, which carries no such restriction.

## Planned change

Keep the existing shape-keyed guard, and change only what the retry does: rewrite the pointer
**in place** via `open("r+b")` + `write()` + `truncate()` instead of `write_bytes`. The chmod
and mode restoration stay, because a genuinely read-only marker is also possible and the
existing mode-restoration contract must hold.

## Portability

The fix is in-process and platform-neutral. It is triggered by the copied marker's bytes, not
by `os.name`, a Windows-specific check, or a CI-provider branch. In-place rewriting is correct
on every platform; it is merely *necessary* on one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The regression test reproduces the defect: it FAILS against pre-fix `_topology_template.py` with a permission error on the read-only `gitdir:` marker, and passes after the fix. Evidence: checkpoint `022-landing-six-fixes-through-gerr.md` records the pre-fix replay failing with the same `PermissionError`, and `test_copy_rewrites_readonly_linked_worktree_git_pointer` passes on `origin/main`.
- [x] `_rewrite_embedded_paths()` restores the pointer file's original mode after writing, verified by asserting the mode before and after. Evidence: `_write_rewritten_path()` in `tests/_topology_template.py` saves `mode`, writes with `stat.S_IWUSR`, and restores `path.chmod(mode)` in `finally`, while `test_copy_rewrites_readonly_linked_worktree_git_pointer` asserts the copied marker still has no write bits.
- [x] The guard keys on the `gitdir:` byte prefix of a `.git` file, not on `os.name` or any platform check. Evidence: `tests/_topology_template.py` guards on `path.name == ".git"` and `original.startswith(b"gitdir:")`, and the file contains no platform branch for this path.
- [x] Non-`.git` metadata files follow the unchanged write path, verified by an existing-behaviour test. Evidence: `_rewrite_embedded_paths()` still calls `path.write_bytes(data)` first for all rewritten files and re-raises `PermissionError` for non-`.git`/non-`gitdir:` files; `test_fully_fixed_copy_is_self_contained` passes unchanged.
- [x] `pytest tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py` passes. Evidence: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py -p no:randomly -q` passed with `14 passed in 13.51s` in the detached `origin/main` worktree.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass. Evidence: both commands passed in the detached `origin/main` worktree; Ruff reported all checks/formats clean and mypy reported success in `770` source files.
- [x] `make verify` shows no new failures beyond the known environmental set. Evidence: Gerrit Verified Gate run `35526996216` for change `3015` patchset 1 completed `success`, including lint/type-check and the CI gating pytest matrix for rev `fba0d8ce2b0`.
- [x] The retry does not reopen the marker with a creating mode. A test denies `Path.write_bytes` for the marker on EVERY call — standing in for the Windows refusal that chmod cannot clear — and asserts the rewrite still succeeds having attempted `write_bytes` exactly once. Oracle: `tests/unit/test_topology_template_gitdir_rewrite_d724.py::test_retry_rewrites_in_place_when_recreating_stays_denied`, which must fail against pre-fix code at `tests/_topology_template.py:212: path.write_bytes(data)` — the exact line and call that fails in Windows CI — and pass after. Evidence: merged to `main` as Gerrit change 3025 (`ca90e8511df`, `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`); `pytest tests/unit/test_topology_template_gitdir_rewrite_d724.py -p no:randomly -q` reports `4 passed`.
- [x] The in-place write truncates, so a longer original leaves no trailing bytes. Oracle: `tests/unit/test_topology_template_gitdir_rewrite_d724.py::test_truncation_leaves_no_trailing_bytes_from_a_longer_original`, red pre-fix and green after. Evidence: merged to `main` as Gerrit change 3025 (`ca90e8511df`, `Verified +1` and `LLM-Review +1`); `pytest tests/unit/test_topology_template_gitdir_rewrite_d724.py -p no:randomly -q` reports `4 passed`.
- [x] The Windows advisory sweep run after this lands no longer reports `test_copy_rewrites_readonly_linked_worktree_git_pointer` in the `.tickets-tracker\.git` `PermissionError` class. Evidence: sweep run `35572919806` job `106248614492` at `1b3bf5ffd1f`; see the comment "Windows sweep confirms the fix". [non-codebase]
  provenance: environment=github-actions windows-latest sweep; principal=rebar CI workflow `test.yml` job `sweep (windows)`; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — no Windows host is available locally, so the only instrument for the hidden-attribute behaviour is a dispatched sweep on the same runner image that produced the failure.

## Validation status

The in-place change MERGED to `main` as Gerrit change 3025 (`ca90e8511df`) with `LLM-Review +1`
and `Verified +1`. The three new-behaviour tests were proven red against pre-fix code and green
after, and pass on merged `main`. Only the Windows advisory-sweep criterion remains.

## Scope of the sweep criterion — deliberately narrowed

The criterion formerly asked that the whole `.tickets-tracker\.git` `PermissionError` CLASS
disappear. That is unsatisfiable and was never this ticket's scope: run `35530066749` shows
8 distinct tests producing that class, and 7 of them are the `.git`-is-a-directory assumptions
this ticket's own "Out of scope" section already excludes. Only
`test_copy_rewrites_readonly_linked_worktree_git_pointer` is this ticket's regression test, so
only that one is in scope.

Note also that the Windows sweep is `continue-on-error: true` and non-gating, and Windows is
broadly red there (1645 failed, 1383 errors in that run). A green sweep is not an achievable
signal; the achievable signal is that this one test stops appearing.

## Out of scope

The MAX_PATH policy decision, whether the Windows sweep should be a gate, the other Windows
failure classes, and unrelated test-only `.git`-is-a-directory assumptions remain outside this
ticket.
